dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi, yes. This is Gina Santoro. I'm calling about a manhole cover. It has sunk, down in the road, and every time a car goes over it, it rings. Bang, clang, like a big metal pot lid.
Oh, that's an awful noise to live with. Okay, a sunken manhole cover. Where is this, Mrs. Santoro?
It's right in front of my house. Two fifty-seven Bellevue Avenue. Over by the stone wall, a little past the corner.
Two fifty-seven Bellevue Avenue. Let me type that in. And the cover is in the street itself, not on your property or the sidewalk?
The street. In the travel lane, on my side. Cars hit it all day. I hear it from the kitchen, from the front room, everywhere. Sorry, hold on one second.
Sure, take your time.
[pause] Sorry. I've got a pot of sauce on and the burner is wicked close to the, um, the counter. It's a very small kitchen, there's no room to turn around. Anyway. Where was I.
The cover, in the travel lane, on your side of the street. That's fine, I've got that. How long has it been sunk down like this?
Since the cold snap, I'd say. A few weeks. At first it was a little clunk. Now it's a real clang. The pavement around it has dropped, you see, so the cover sits up higher than the road.
So the asphalt has settled around it and the cover is sticking up. Is that right? Or is the cover itself down below the road?
No, no, the pavement is down. The cover is up. Like a little hump, I mean, a ridge on the edge. You feel it when you drive.
Okay, got it. Pavement dipped around the cover, cover sitting proud, and it bangs when cars cross. Has anyone had any damage from it that you know of?
Well, my neighbor hit it. The man next door, he came over and told me. He hit it with his tire and he said it jolted the whole car. He was not happy about it. I told him I'd call, so here I am.
Did he say whether anything on the car got damaged?
He didn't say. He said it rattled him, that's all I know. I'm not going to guess about his car.
That's fair. I'll note that a neighbor reported hitting it. Is it near a driveway, or is there a hydrant close by? Anything the crew can use to find it?
It's about even with my mailbox. The mailbox is the black one, with the number on the post. Right across from the big hedge.
Even with the black mailbox, across from the hedge. Good. And is the cover a round one, as far as you can tell?
Round. Iron, I think. Heavy looking. It's got a pattern on top, little squares.
Okay. Mrs. Santoro, is that a number I can reach you at if the crew needs to check anything? I have it as four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-nine. Is that right?
Yes, that's the landline. Oh-one-six-nine. I'm home most of the day, so somebody will pick up.

Perfect. Let me read this back. Sunken pavement around a round manhole cover in the travel lane in front of two fifty-seven Bellevue Avenue, even with your mailbox, cover sticks up and rings when cars cross, neighbor also hit it. Did I get all that?
That's it. That's the whole story. Now, how long does a repair usually take? Because I have been listening to this for weeks, and I'd like to know if I'm going to hear it all month.

I understand. Usually it starts with someone going out to look at it, and then it gets scheduled with the other road work. This time of year, the crews are busy with winter patching, so it could be a week or two to get someone out, and the actual fix may take a bit after that depending on whether it's the cover or the pavement.
A week or two. Then more after that. Well. That's not what I was hoping to hear, but I suppose it is what it is.
I know, it's not a quick answer. The cold can make it harder too, because the asphalt doesn't set well in freezing weather. Sometimes they put down a temporary patch first.
A temporary patch. Fine. As long as it stops the clanging. I can't hear my own radio over it.
I'll mark it so they know it's noisy and a hazard to cars, so it gets looked at sooner rather than later. If somebody does go out and it's different from what you described, they may call you.
All right. And if I don't hear anything, can I call back?
Absolutely. Just give the address, two fifty-seven Bellevue, and say you called about the manhole cover. Whoever answers can look it up.
Two fifty-seven Bellevue, manhole cover. Okay. I'll write that on the pad by the phone.
Good idea. Anything else I can help with today?
No, that's all. My sauce is going to burn. Thank you, Lorraine.
You're welcome, Mrs. Santoro. Have a good afternoon.
You too. Goodbye.
